channel.title: AAE Updates for Windows
channel.description: Updates for AAE, the Accessible Android Emulator, on Windows.

item.title: Version 0.4.0
item.description:
• AAE Remote, a new Android app, uses this computer's devices from your phone: their sound and vibrations play on the phone, and you manage and use them with keyboard and gesture modes and the testing tools. Turn on File, Serve Devices to Phones, then pair your phone with the code AAE shows.
  • AAE can serve devices whenever you log in, without being open.
  • Quitting while a device is stopping now waits for it, so its emulator isn't left running.
  • Speak Status names the screen reader, and an app made only for ARM processors gets a clear message when it can't install.

item.title: Version 0.3.1
item.description:
• Devices are much faster: they now draw their screens with the computer's graphics adapter. Before, the emulator drew them in software, on the processor.
  • Speech no longer fails on a device's first start when the speech engine is slow to answer.
  • AAE says when a computer is below what it needs, and gives devices fewer processor cores on small processors.
  • Diagnostic reports name the processor and graphics, and keep more personal details out.

item.title: Version 0.3.0
item.description:
• The Windows app now has the Mac app's windows: Accessibility Inspector (Control Alt I), Speech Log (Control Alt L), Device Log (Control Alt J), Shell (Control Alt T), Apps (Control Alt P), Accessibility Services (Control Alt U), Snapshots (Control Alt S), Battery, Location and Phone (Control Alt B), Android Versions (Control Alt A), Open Link (Control Shift L), Send Intent, and Watch for New Builds.
  • Open in Own Window (Control Alt O) gives a device a window of its own; the menu's shortcuts act on it while it's in front.
  • Tab no longer gets stuck in the set-up text or the last message, and the focus is never left nowhere when a button becomes unavailable.
